headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults make prompt injection, data leakage, and workflow corruption plausible across Continue and Kestra.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP; Kestra can read/write files and process workflow inputs. Because both share filesystem-based state and Continue may ingest file content as trusted context, attacker-controlled content from one side can influence the other. This is not provably blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or storage path
IF Kestra writes attacker-controlled text into files that Continue later opens
IF Continue routes file content into MCP/tool prompts without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP servers that ingest untrusted files
Add a manual review step before Continue reads Kestra-generated artifacts
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between workflow outputs and IDE inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code, open editor buffers, and model-provider API keys, while Kestra handles logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and notifications. With shared filesystem state and broad network egress on both sides, sensitive data can flow from one agent into the other and then out to external services without a default containment boundary.
conditions: IF Continue opens files containing secrets, credentials, or proprietary code
IF Kestra stores those same files or derived artifacts in /app/storage or /tmp
IF either agent forwards shared content to a remote model provider or external API
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace files
Restrict network egress for both agents to approved endpoints
Use separate service accounts and credentials
Rotate any API keys exposed in editor buffers
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering between workspace and workflow storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network capabilities. Continue explicitly shares state via filesystem across IDE instances, and Kestra supports multiple instances plus writes to storage paths. That creates a direct write-write conflict on shared mutable resources, with potential corruption of code, workflows, or artifacts.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory tree
IF Kestra tasks and Continue edits target the same files concurrently
IF no external locking or checkout isolation is configured
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Use file locks or single-writer scheduling
Run one agent in read-only mode
Pause one agent during the other's write window
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code, commands, or file edits that Kestra may consume as workflow inputs or artifacts. Kestra then has downstream action-taking authority over email, Slack, cloud, and infrastructure surfaces, so an unchecked mistake from Continue can cascade into real-world actions. The profiles do not show a verification gate that would block this by default.
conditions: IF Kestra uses Continue-produced files or text as workflow definitions
IF those workflows trigger notifications, cloud actions, or deployments
IF no human approval or schema validation occurs before execution
mitigations: Require manual approval before Kestra runs Continue-generated workflows
Validate generated files against schema before execution
Limit Kestra to dry-run mode for generated inputs
Keep Continue outputs in a staging directory
requires-engineering: add signed handoff artifacts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is an IDE assistant touching source code and editor buffers, while Kestra processes logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data. If regulated data is placed into shared files or workflows, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across two different operational stacks. No compliance boundary is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in shared workspace files
IF Kestra persists those files or derived artifacts longer than Continue's editor session
IF the deployment spans jurisdictions or retention regimes with different obligations
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files
Set explicit retention limits on Kestra storage
Delete transient artifacts after each run
Document data-flow ownership for both tools
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across the pair
